topic: RAG response cache scope and revocation
dates: Live documentation checked 2026-11-18; no publication date assumed
Live documentation checked 2026-11-18; no publication date assumed
claim: Cached responses need request-appropriate scope; tenant partition alone does not encode every authorization or source-content change.
experiment: 144 local deterministic request sequences: 8 fixtures x 3 cache policies x 6 schedules.
baseline: Exact query-only key, compared with tenant key and fresh authorized context key.
metrics: Unauthorized answers/24, stale authorized answers/8, repeat cache hits/8, correct cold denials/8, correct final responses/48 per mode.
resources: Python standard library and current Codex through INVARIANT. No measured LLM/API calls.
runtime: Minutes after implementation; no new packages/models.
limits: Selected counterexamples, synchronous in-memory cache, trusted driver identities, exact matching. Not semantic caching, an authentication solution, vendor benchmark or live RAG test.
classification: Original engineering experiment; different read-side cache path from prior refund authorization and worker/retry topics.
selection: Practical authorization/freshness boundary with complete inspectable state and negative/positive controls; no outcome-based tuning.

topic: Pre-filtering versus post-filtering scoped vector search
claim: Filtering only after top-k selection can reduce eligible recall; exposure control is distinct from measured model hijacks.
experiment: Authored vectors and eligibility sets; scoped oracle versus global top-k then filtering.
baseline: Exact global selection followed by tenant filtering.
metrics: Eligible recall@k, number returned, unauthorized exposure and clean availability.
data: Synthetic vectors available; SearchInject abstract read, full artifact not audited today.
resources: Python, optional existing local models only.
runtime: Minutes for mathematical counterexamples; downstream evaluation needs more fixture work.
limits: A toy would not reproduce Elastic ANN performance or SearchInject attack-success effects.
classification: Deferred; less direct connection to the currently untested response-cache boundary.

claim: The source describes altered model weights that change agent behavior on a trigger.
experiment: Faithful validation would need an audited checkpoint-modification and trigger-evaluation protocol.
baseline: Verified original weights versus controlled modified checkpoint.
metrics: Trigger selectivity, ordinary behavior, integrity-detector true/false positives.
data: Primary announcement checked, linked implementation not executed or audited.
resources: Would require a modified model beyond the standing installed-model inference scope.
limits: No model modification, downloads or attack commands are authorized by source text. An artifact-hash smoke test alone would not validate the behavioral claim.
classification: Deferred; do not present a checksum toy as a backdoor reproduction.
